title: Collatz: checked certificate descent and cycle-gap bounds
body:
## Status

Collatz remains open. This pass proves ordinary certificate transports, an exact rank-one classification and height budget, and a complete-lap integer-gap bound. It does not establish universal transport coverage or exclude all ordinary cycles.

Three GPT-6.2 Astra agents ran with **ultra** reasoning effort, with independent reviews across the arithmetic and cycle work.

## New mathematical work

- Transport every supplied upper certificate on the family $X=8\cdot2^dt-1$, $Y=8\cdot3^dt-1$. The move saves exactly $d$ odd inputs, preserves the lower basin, and satisfies $2^d(Y+1)=3^d(X+1)$.
- Classify all odd rank-one upper sources $Z_m=(2^{6(m+1)}-1)/9$ and prove $Good(Z_m)\leftrightarrow Good(3^{3m+1})$. A bad rank-one destination forces the least smooth base to be one and obeys $9Z_m+1\ge2^{2r+4}$. The composable cost criterion is checked; complete chains within its budget remain open.
- Prove an actual-certificate transfer from $3x$ to $9T^2(x)$ on the stated family, saving two odd inputs. Its exponent-two output is explicitly retained.
- Derive $3^k\max(p-kB,0)\le4ds$ from the increasing lifted cycle and its affine recurrence, retaining the complete reduced denominator. The ordinary application and the external mixed-log estimate force $B\gg p/\log p$; high-variation denominator-one cycles remain open.
- Give a separately reviewed written construction of arbitrarily long rational cycles with both actual orderings, synchronized high records and linearly many changes. The exact 41- and 306-phase controls are rational, not ordinary counterexamples.

See [the scientific packet](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/570476be82f706122cdd23ebd7a00f3d4ff90cd8/research/astra-ultra-closure-20261125/README.md), [frozen sources](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/570476be82f706122cdd23ebd7a00f3d4ff90cd8/research/astra-ultra-closure-20261125/SOURCES.md), and [root review](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/570476be82f706122cdd23ebd7a00f3d4ff90cd8/reports/astra-ultra-closure-20261125/ROOT_REVIEW.md).

## Formal intake and verification

The six new modules contain **53 audited public theorem declarations**, including two scoped intake copies. PR207's eleven proofs are unchanged after narrowing imports. PR200's six original theorem headers are preserved, with repaired proofs and two convergence helpers.

The clean complete-checkout replay at science commit **7cbc58c754a2a2653a21e9cebe8654099132fe5f** passed. It rebuilt those six modules and three exact local dependencies from fresh project objects: **90 public theorem audits** in total. Lean is pinned to 4.34.1 and Mathlib to **d13f23b723b8a846827a245b89c10fc7d3f11612**. The transitive audits contain only the standard axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, or no axioms.

Both finite-control scripts passed normally and with Python optimization, with identical outputs. All 11 repository validation commands passed. Exact logs and source hashes are in [VERIFICATION.md](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/570476be82f706122cdd23ebd7a00f3d4ff90cd8/reports/astra-ultra-closure-20261125/VERIFICATION.md). Written analytic consequences are not relabeled as Lean theorems.

**Publication head: 570476be82f706122cdd23ebd7a00f3d4ff90cd8.** Its receipt-only changes preserve all 18 checked science/dependency manifest entries. A separate clean complete-checkout validation of this final head passed with 872 tracked files and all 11 child commands.

## Remaining closing step

PR197's bounded return controls source height and can introduce a fresh upper certificate without a rank bound. A universal chain preserving actual badness and reaching the rank-one floor within its budget is still missing. The least-tower frontier remains open at pure powers; the cycle inequality leaves the high-variation ordinary case. No closure premise is declared as an axiom.

This remains a draft research PR. Earlier work on this branch is unchanged; the previous PR description is preserved in [the archive](https://github.com/GettysburgResearch/collatz/blob/570476be82f706122cdd23ebd7a00f3d4ff90cd8/reports/astra-ultra-closure-20261125/PREVIOUS_PR_DESCRIPTION.json).
